uncited: A 16-bit floating-point HDR rendering pipeline for scene post-processing that applies HDR-domain effects, tone mapping, and LDR-domain effects in a fused shader pass to minimize memory bandwidth.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Cloud Compositing & Tone Mapping](3628-cloud-compositing-tone-mapping.md) by integrating bloom and chromatic distortion directly into the tone-mapping fragment shader rather than using separate library passes, and from [Bloom](4906-bloom.md) by handling the bloom compositing within the same pass as tone mapping.
Multisampling (MSAA, SSAA) and FXAA are off by default.
- Tone Map Operators: Enum selecting LINEAR, REINHARD, CINEON, ACES filmic (default), AgX, or NEUTRAL.
Render the scene into a HalfFloat target.
Apply HDR-domain effects (mipmap-based bloom, chromatic lens distortion, physically based detector noise).
Bloom compositing: Mix bloom into the HDR sample.
Chromatic distortion: Apply per-channel chromatic sampling.
Tone mapping: Apply the selected tone map operator with exposure, additive offset, and gamma.
- Tone Map Operator: LINEAR, REINHARD, CINEON, ACES filmic (default), AgX, NEUTRAL.
NEUTRAL is an alias of LINEAR; both clamp to [0, 1].
- Adaptive device-pixel-ratio scaling is locked during recording to prevent mid-capture resolution changes.
- The probe-and-verify guard reverts a downscale if it does not actually improve throughput.
- Time Complexity: Not given in the sources.
- Memory Complexity: Not given in the sources.
- Measured Performance: Not given in the sources.

- Scaling: Adaptive device-pixel-ratio scaling monitors a 1 s sliding window of frame timestamps and adjusts the render-target resolution using thresholds set relative to the display’s estimated achievable refresh rate.
- When to use: When HDR-domain effects and tone mapping are needed with minimal overhead.
- When not to use: When recording, as adaptive scaling is locked.
The HDR Post-Processing Pipeline is part of the Luxar system for Gaussian splatting for microscopy and scalable interactive web visualisation of multidimensional scientific data.
It was introduced in a preprint by the author/funder, who granted bioRxiv a license to display the preprint in perpetuity.
